label: Viral
about: Built to hold attention: long pauses gone but your natural rhythm kept, bold word-by-word captions, and framing that changes on the cuts so they feel deliberate.
editor_notes: Judgement pass, because the automatic version only sees words. (1) The first 1-3 seconds decide everything: open on a specific claim, number, result or question, with a 2-5 word hook title that adds to the line rather than repeating it. Replace the automatic teaser if a better line exists, or remove it if the opening is already strong. (2) One idea per video; cut anything that doesn't serve it, aiming for 20-45 s. (3) Keep it easy to follow: never cut a pause just because it exists, keep sentences whole, and change the framing on cuts rather than in the middle of a thought. Add graphics or B-roll where the words call for them, not on a timer. (4) End on the payoff with no fade or sign-off, so it can loop. (5) Don't promise views: this improves the odds of holding attention, and the idea matters more than the edit.
